Conversation, family & daily routines

fall on deaf ears phrase

also preach to deaf ears, you’re preaching to deaf ears, talk to a brick wall, to preach to deaf ears

classical

Liv. 40.8.10 (Lewis & Short s.v. surdus)
Verg. Ecl. 10.8: nōn canimus surdīs (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 40.8.10: quae vereor nē vāna surdīs auribus cecinerim (Lewis & Short s.v. canō)

surdīs auribus canere

sing to deaf ears: talk in vain

The deaf ears stand in the dative, with no preposition.

Other words

  • ad surdās aurēs cantāre — preach to deaf ears

    also used · classical · Ov. Am. 3.7.61 (Lewis & Short s.v. cantō: “to preach to deaf ears”); Traupman 96, 255, 301

    Traupman’s form, with ad. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

  • Nōn canimus surdīs. — we are not singing to the deaf

    also used · classical · Verg. Ecl. 10.8 (Lewis & Short s.v. canō)

Examples

  • quae vereor nē vāna surdīs auribus cecinerim

    which I fear I have sung in vain to deaf earsLiv. 40.8.10 (Lewis & Short)

SourcesQuotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
